title: Interoception in adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury
summary: The study investigates whether the ability to feel one's own body (interoception) differs between adolescets with and without non-suicidal self-injurious behavior. In addition two influencing factors are examined: emotional pictures which induce strong negative feelings (and decrease interoception) and a mindfulness exercise that helps to focus on the whole body (and improves interoception).  It is assumed that adolescents with non-suicidal self-injurious behavior are influenced more or differently by arousal and mindfulness.

interventions.name:
Patients with non-suicidal self-injury take part in an appointment lasting around 2.5 hours and consisting of:
1) a structured clinical examination with psychometric methods and
2) a measurement of interoception at rest, after arousal and after a one-time mindfulness intervention

Healthy control group, which also takes part in a single appointment consisting of:
1) a structured clinical examination with psychometric methods and
2) a measurement of interoception at rest, after arousal and after a one-time mindfulness intervention
